root_cause.text: In the e1000/e1000e TX DMA mapping error path, `count` was decremented before the `while (count--)` cleanup loop, creating an off-by-one bug that skipped unmapping one already-mapped TX buffer when `dma_error` was reached.
root_cause.evidence: The patch removes `if (count) count--;` from `e1000_tx_map()` in both `drivers/net/ethernet/intel/e1000/e1000_main.c` and `drivers/net/ethernet/intel/e1000e/netdev.c`, and the CVE text says `count` is already incremented after each successful mapping so pre-decrementing it “causes an off-by-one error” and “exactly one DMA mapping would leak.”

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix TX DMA error cleanup to unwind the full set of mapped buffers.
intent_record.what: In the TX DMA mapping error path of `e1000_tx_map()`, the conditional `if (count) count--;` was removed immediately before the `while (count--)` cleanup loop.
intent_record.how: On a DMA mapping failure, the cleanup loop now starts with the original `count` value instead of one less, so one additional previously mapped TX buffer entry will be unwound and released during error handling.

intent_record.what: The code removes a conditional decrement of `count` in the `dma_error` path of `e1000_tx_map()`. Specifically, the lines `if (count) count--;` were deleted before the `while (count--)` cleanup loop.
